questions: If there are multiple possible final contiguous intervals of 1s that can be achieved with the same minimal number of swaps, does the answer depend on which interval is chosen, or is the answer simply the minimal number of swaps needed to achieve any such interval?
Are adjacent swaps allowed to cross the boundary of the string, i.e., can we swap the N-th and (N+1)-th characters (which doesn't exist)?
If the string already has all 1s contiguous, is the answer 0?
When counting operations, is each swap of two adjacent characters counted as one operation, regardless of whether the same character is swapped multiple times?
Does the final contiguous block of 1s have to be in a specific position (e.g., as left as possible) or can it be anywhere?
If there are no '1's in the string, is the condition 'all 1s are contiguous' considered true vacuously, and thus the answer is 0?
Are we allowed to swap characters that are both '0' or both '1', and if so, do such swaps count towards the total operations even though they don't change the string?

Is the string indexed starting from 1 or 0? The problem statement uses 1-based indexing (i-th character, l and r from 1 to N), but implementations typically use 0-based. Does this affect the answer calculation?
